archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (paint-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose point margin and efficiency play like a middle-of-the-pack side, with a 2-4 start that reflects close losses more than its level, built on Zion Williamson's interior scoring rather than the three-point line.

report.headline: A 2-4 start that hides a break-even team still fighting its weak spots
report.take:
The Pelicans arrive off two dismal seasons, 21-61 and then 26-56, and six games into 2026-27 they do not look like that team. Their Net Rtg of 1.8 ranks 14th, the offense (16th) and defense (13th) both sit near the middle, and they have outscored opponents by 11 points on the season. The record says 2-4 because of how the losses came: 120-123 to Indiana, 119-120 in Utah, and 135-141 in overtime in Denver. The margin implies three wins rather than two, and the W vs Pt Diff of -1 is the gap. Close losses like these mostly even out.

The identity is unusual for the modern game. New Orleans takes the smallest share of its shots from three in the league (3PA Rate 32.8, 30th) and makes them poorly (31.2%, 25th), yet ranks third in TS % at 60. That comes from the paint and the line. The FT Rate of 35.3 is fourth, and Zion Williamson is scoring at a 69.4 TS % with 124 points, ranked 9th of 85 on the power forward tab. The frontcourt grades A-, with Derik Queen, Karlo Matković and Yves Missi all efficient around him. The backcourt grade is B- and the wings C-, so the offense runs through the bigs.

Some of the numbers flatter the defense. Opponents are shooting 30.5% from three, fifth-best, against a 35.0% mark allowed last year, and that figure tends to drift back toward the league. The underlying problem is at the rim: opponents shoot 71.8% there (27th), and opposing centers have produced more points, rebounds and assists combined than against any other team. The defensive rating of 111.4 is well ahead of last year's 118.9, but expect some of that gain to fade. The ball-handling has also gotten worse. TOV % has climbed to 15.8 (26th) from 12.2 last season, and Jeremiah Fears (50.1 TS %, -3.9 BPM) has carried heavy usage while Dejounte Murray has played only four games and Jordan Poole is out.

The direction is encouraging. After an 0-4 start the Pelicans won 132-120 over Sacramento and 121-99 over Atlanta. If the close games break more evenly, this looks like a team that can hover around the play-in line. That would be a real step forward from where the franchise has been. A team this dependent on free throws and one star's efficiency, and this weak at the rim, still has to prove it over a bigger sample.

strengths.title: Efficient scoring without the three
strengths.body: New Orleans ranks third in TS % despite the league's lowest three-point volume, because it lives at the free-throw line and finishes inside. Zion Williamson's 69.4 TS % sets the tone. The free-throw rate is a repeatable trait of a paint-heavy offense. Williamson's efficiency will likely come down some from this level.

strengths.title: A deep, productive frontcourt
strengths.body: The frontcourt grades A-, the best group on the roster. Queen has 47 rebounds, Matković is shooting a 74 TS % off the bench, and Missi ranks 3rd on the center tab in his two games. The frontcourt's listed players lead the team in Win Shares. This depth also covers for the thin guard rotation.

strengths.title: Finishing possessions on the glass
strengths.body: A DRB % of 76.4 ranks 6th, so opponents rarely get second chances. That is a meaningful improvement on last year's 71.4, and it follows from playing big lineups. It should hold better than the three-point defense will.

concerns.title: Getting carved up at the rim
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 71.8% within four feet, 27th in the league, and opposing centers have feasted, with the league's worst figures allowed to the position. The big lineups win the glass but do not deter shots. This is the flaw most likely to define the defense once the opponents' three-point luck evens out.

concerns.title: No spacing from the perimeter
concerns.body: The 3PA Rate trails the league by 10 points, and the threes the Pelicans do take fall at 31.2%. The wings grade C-, so defenses can pack the paint against Williamson. Unless the shooting improves, this offense has little margin when the free throws dry up.

concerns.title: Turnovers and shaky guard play
concerns.body: TOV % of 15.8 ranks 26th, well above last season's rate. Fears has handled a large share of possessions at a 50.1 TS % and -3.9 BPM, and Poole is out. Murray's return to a fuller role is the likeliest fix.

trend.note: An 0-4 start of narrow and overtime losses gave way to two comfortable home wins. The last five games ran slightly better than the season in margin and points allowed.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, two contenders, and a back-to-back to close
weekAhead.body:
The week opens in Memphis against the site's top-ranked team, unbeaten with a 15.1 Net Rtg. Minnesota, ranked 5th with a top-four defense, visits later in the week. Utah and the Clippers are both 1-5 and rank in the bottom five on the site. The week ends with a back-to-back at the Clippers and then at Golden State, which is the real test of depth with Murphy listed day-to-day and Poole out.

The bright spot is that three of these opponents leak at the rim. The Clippers and Warriors rank 27th and 29th in Opp Rim FG %, which suits a team that lives in the paint. Memphis and Minnesota guard the paint and the glass far better, and Memphis has held power forwards to almost nothing. A 3-2 week would be a good result. Splitting the two winnable games would undo the recent momentum.

keyMatchups.title: Zion against Memphis's power-forward wall
keyMatchups.body: Memphis has allowed 10 points a game to power forwards, second-fewest in the league. It also limits rim attempts (Opp Rim Rate 24.9, 5th). Williamson is the offense, so this is the hardest version of his matchup all week.

keyMatchups.title: Pressure on a careless Clippers team
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers turn it over more than anyone (TOV % 18.4, 30th) and allow a 57.0 Opp eFG %. The Pelicans force turnovers at a top-ten rate. This is the game where the interior attack and the transition chances should both be there.

keyMatchups.title: Warriors' threes versus Pelicans' paint
keyMatchups.body: Golden State shoots 40% from three on heavy volume but allows 73.1% at the rim and has a D- frontcourt. The Pelicans' strong three-point defense numbers get tested here. On the other end, the Warriors' soft interior suits Williamson and Queen, even at the end of a back-to-back.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Pelicans protect the rim against Memphis and Minnesota bigs. Opposing centers have had their way, and those two teams can punish it.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin says this is roughly a .500-caliber team in a strong division. Two parts of the season look durable: the free-throw rate and the defensive rebounding. The 30.5% three-point shooting allowed is the number most likely to regress, and when it does, the weak rim protection will show more in the defensive rating. Better luck in close games should offset some of that, as should healthier guard play if Murray and Poole stabilize the backcourt.

The current 27-win pace reflects the four close losses more than the team's level, so expect the record to rise. Even so, the lack of shooting and the turnover problem cap the upside. A finish in the low-to-mid 30s in wins, contending for a play-in spot, is the realistic band. The improvement over last season's 26 wins would be clear but not dramatic.
swingFactors: Rim protection as opponents' three-point shooting normalizes
Murray and Poole stabilizing the guard minutes and turnovers

confidence.note: Six games, with several key players in small or injury-limited samples.
